The finding uses this to declare the doc-goc §5 worry ('curation may filter out warning-list / qualified-audit names, so blind replacement degrades the universe') as 'not supported by the data' — but §5's worry is precisely about subtraction, and a test that can only observe subtraction has zero power against it. I refute that claim, not the project. The plan's actual direction survives independently and comfortably: circular selection bias is confirmed by bq_admin's own answer (hit_ticker_list derives from profile_hit.csv, i.e. backtest deals), non-reproducibility is confirmed (IVS 0 to 1.622 rows in 8 days, and I watched n_union drift 459 to 381 myself), look-ahead is real and in fact larger than quoted (2,7x not 2,3x, since the D1 pattern has no time predicate at all), and the CAPIT breadth-denominator hazard is verified in code at golive_recommend_v23.py:655/96/430. Credit where due: the self-flagged n=1 sweep risk resolves in Taylor's favour when I extend it to 2018 and 2022, the refusal to accept the 'ETL bugs are irrelevant' assumption is vindicated by the original QA text, and §8.4's warning about self-tuning a universe for a system whose history is known is exactly the right instinct — which is why §2.2's overclaim needs correcting before it hardens into fleet consensus. Recommend proceeding with Q1/Q3/Q4/Q5 on the confirmed grounds, and rewriting §2.2 so that no future reader cites 97-99% as proof that curation was uninformative."}
